schedule.schedule_summary: Recurrent-disease temozolomide orally once daily on Days 1–5 of each 28-day cycle, then 23 days without temozolomide. Initial dose 200 mg/m² if chemotherapy-naive or 150 mg/m² after prior chemotherapy; any cycle 2 increase needs haematological and prescribing review.
schedule.duration_text: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; no fixed six-cycle cap is established by the recurrent-treatment paragraph.

components.dose: 150 or 200 mg/m² once daily according to prior chemotherapy and toxicity history
components.note: 23 days without temozolomide follow each five-day course. The recurrent regimen does not use a six-cycle cap. Take fasting; swallow whole. Do not repeat a dose after vomiting. Confirm missed-dose advice with the treatment team.

schedule.administration: Fasting; swallow whole with water. Do not open or chew capsules. Do not repeat a dose after vomiting. NCCP missed-dose instruction: take the missed dose unless the next dose is due within 12 hours; confirm instructions with the treating pharmacist.

each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile onDay 1 before each course
smPC_supplement: CBC onDay 22 (±48 hours), then weekly until ANC >1.5×10⁹/L and platelets >100×10⁹/L
LFTs after each cycle; toxicity may occur weeks or more after the last dose
monitoring.disease_monitoring: Imaging and other disease tests according to the individual consultant plan; no fixed MRI interval is imposed by this NCCP regimen.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: NCCP 00342 v 4 p 3 classifies temozolomide as oral moderate to high emetogenic potential; antiemetics on the five oral-treatment days according to local policy, not a routine 28-day antiemetic course.
other_supportive_care: Take temozolomide fasting and swallow capsules whole with water; do not open or chew.
Do not repeat a dose after vomiting. Confirm the NCCP missed-dose instruction with oncology pharmacy.
Review antiemetic control on treatment days and after prior severe vomiting.

NCCP advises men not to father a child for six months after the last dose; EMA currently states at least three months. Confirm the Irish plan with the treating team. Discuss sperm preservation before treatment.
EMA advises effective contraception for women during treatment and for at least six months after completion.
Review HBV results and the liver-specialist plan when serology is positive.
Review seizure medicines, corticosteroids and other marrow-suppressive medicines; do not stop them without the treating team.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
supportive_care.pjp_prophylaxis: Risk-based review for this five-day recurrent monotherapy schedule. All TMZ patients, particularly with corticosteroids or lymphopenia, need PJP vigilance. Universal prophylaxis for 42-day concomitantRT belongs to a different regimen.

source_conflicts.resolution: Significant hepatic dysfunction is an NCCP exclusion; Table 3 says no adjustment is expected for Child-Pugh C. Flag the conflict for consultant/pharmacy decision; Child-Pugh C must not yield automatic standard-dose clearance.

Predose criteria use ANC ≥1.5/platelets≥100, but weekly recovery monitoring continues until ANC >1.5/platelets >100. Exact equality after a cytopenic episode requires review; do not infer complete recovery from the predose threshold alone.

urgent_symptoms: Fever or feeling acutely unwell, particularly with low blood counts
New or worsening breathlessness/cough, especially during steroid treatment
Yellow eyes/skin, dark urine or new severe abdominal symptoms
Severe vomiting or inability to keep fluids/medicines down
New seizure, weakness, marked confusion or deteriorating neurological symptoms require urgent clinical assessment; do not assume they are only a medicine effect
anatomical_anchors: Lungs/infection: opportunistic infection/PJP risk; not universal prophylaxis for this regimen
Skin/hair: rash/hair loss; severe reactions need urgent help
Energy/brain symptoms: fatigue, headache and drowsiness can overlap with tumour/steroids; report change
Fertility/reproduction: avoid pregnancy; discuss sperm preservation and source-specific contraception advice
indication_boundary: NCCP adult recurrent/progressive GradeIII/IV glioma. Glioma patient education must not expand treatment eligibility or set an arbitrary six-cycle duration.
